name: Neon Starter Pack
author: NeonSec content team (fictional)
description: Two synthetic analysis labs that demonstrate the lab pack format: a DNS beacon review and a storage policy review. Fictional organizations and documentation address ranges only.

labs.title: Pack Lab: Fixed-Interval DNS Lookups
labs.brief: A synthetic resolver log from a fictional workstation shows repeated lookups. Decide whether they look automated and recommend containment. Log review only.

allowed: The synthetic resolver log in this pack
Local notes and the report builder
forbidden: Any real resolver, domain, or host
Any external lookup of the listed names

labs.evidence:
2026-06-02T09:00:00Z 10.40.8.21 query A updates.neonharbor.example NOERROR
2026-06-02T09:05:00Z 10.40.8.21 query A cdn-7f.beacon-demo.invalid NOERROR
2026-06-02T09:10:00Z 10.40.8.21 query A cdn-7f.beacon-demo.invalid NOERROR
2026-06-02T09:15:00Z 10.40.8.21 query A cdn-7f.beacon-demo.invalid NOERROR
2026-06-02T09:16:12Z 10.40.8.30 query A portal.neonharbor.example NOERROR

flagChallenge.prompt: Name the timing pattern shown by the repeated lookups from one workstation and submit it as a flag.

assets.label: resolver-log (synthetic)
assets.description: Prepared resolver queries from fictional hosts.

hints: Compare the timestamps of the repeated name.
The same name is queried exactly every five minutes.
flagChallenge.explanation: One workstation queries the same unfamiliar name every five minutes, a fixed-interval pattern typical of automated check-ins rather than human browsing.
flagChallenge.remediation: Isolate the fictional workstation for triage, block the name at the resolver, and alert on fixed-interval lookups to newly seen names.
flagChallenge.reportPrompt: Write a finding that cites the repeated lookups and recommends containment and detection.

guiding.a: The same fictional name every five minutes from one workstation.

modelFindings.title: Fixed-interval lookups from a fictional workstation
modelFindings.impact: Possible automated check-ins from an unmanaged process.
modelFindings.remediation: Contain the host, block the name, and add interval-based detection.

labs.title: Pack Lab: Storage Policy Review
labs.brief: Review a synthetic storage policy for a fictional logistics tenant and decide what makes the reports container unsafe. Config review only.

allowed: The synthetic storage policy in this pack
Local notes and the report builder

labs.evidence:
container: neonharbor-reports
account: acct-000000-demo
read_access: anyone
list_access: anyone
encryption_at_rest: disabled
access_logging: disabled

flagChallenge.prompt: Identify the most urgent exposure in the storage policy and submit it as a flag.

assets.label: storage-policy (synthetic)
assets.description: Prepared container settings for a fictional tenant.

hints: Who can read and list the container?
flagChallenge.explanation: Anyone can read and list the reports container, so its contents are public; missing encryption and logging make the exposure worse and invisible.
flagChallenge.remediation: Remove anonymous read and list access, enable encryption at rest and access logging, and review which reports were exposed.
flagChallenge.reportPrompt: Write a finding for the public container and a second one for missing encryption and logging.

analysis.detection: Run policy-as-code checks that fail any container granting anonymous read or list access.
analysis.prevention: Block public access by default at the tenant level and require encryption and logging in templates.

guiding.a: Anonymous read and list access: anyone can enumerate and download the reports.

modelFindings.title: Reports container readable and listable by anyone
modelFindings.impact: Fictional customer reports are publicly exposed.
modelFindings.remediation: Remove anonymous access and review exposure.

modelFindings.title: No encryption at rest or access logging
modelFindings.impact: Data is unprotected at rest and access is unaudited.
